# TargetCo Holdings Ltd — Confidential Information Memorandum

**Project Lighthouse — Strictly Confidential**
**Prepared for management review · Sponsor: Marylebone Partners III LP**

This memorandum is fully synthetic — written for fixture use only.
TargetCo Holdings is a fictional entity; any resemblance to real
businesses is coincidental. No real company IP appears here.

## 1. Executive summary

TargetCo Holdings Ltd is a UK-headquartered industrial services group
delivering facilities maintenance, industrial cleaning, mechanical
services, and compliance auditing across a four-segment portfolio.
Founded in Bristol in 1987 by the late Maurice Hambleton, the
business has grown organically and through three small bolt-ons
since 2014 to its present scale.

**Headline financials (FY24, year-ended 31 March 2024):**

- Revenue: £180.0m (+4.0% YoY)
- EBITDA: £24.0m (13.3% margin)
- Adjusted EBITDA (post-management adjustments): £25.6m (14.2% margin)
- Free cash flow: £14.8m (61.7% conversion of EBITDA)
- Headcount: 950 (FTE basis), 88% UK-based
- HQ: Bristol; 12 operational sites across the UK and ROI

The business operates under a tight central-overhead model
(corporate cost stack of 3.4% of revenue) with each segment carrying
its own P&L responsibility under a Group Operations Director.

Founder family ownership is now 22%; Marylebone Partners III LP took
a 71% controlling stake in March 2020 with the residual 7% held by
the present management team under an EMI option pool. The sponsor's
stated exit window opens at 24 months and closes at 36 months.

## 2. Business segments

TargetCo reports across four operating segments. Inter-segment
revenue is immaterial (under 1% of group), so segment numbers below
sum to within rounding of the group total.

### 2.1 Facilities Maintenance (52% of revenue)

The largest segment by revenue. Multi-year master service agreements
with corporate occupiers and building owners covering planned and
reactive maintenance: HVAC, plumbing, electrical, fire suppression,
fabric repair. FY24 revenue £93.6m, EBITDA £13.1m (14.0% margin),
+8.0% YoY. Average contract length 4.7 years, 91% recurring revenue.
Top-10 customer set is stable; the segment lost one £4m contract to
an in-housing trend in FY23 but won £6m of net new in FY24.

### 2.2 Industrial Cleaning (24% of revenue)

Manufacturing, food-production, and pharmaceutical-grade industrial
cleaning. FY24 revenue £43.2m, EBITDA £4.8m (11.1% margin), +2.0%
YoY. Largely transactional revenue (52% one-off jobs, 48% rolling
quarterly contracts). Pharmaceutical-grade cleaning carries the
highest margin (~17%) but is a smaller share of the segment;
manufacturing-grade is competitive and price-led.

The segment's growth has decelerated from 6.0% in FY22 to 2.0% in
FY24 — partly cyclical (industrial customers under cost pressure),
partly competitive (two new regional players in the Midlands).

### 2.3 Mechanical Services (16% of revenue)

Project-based mechanical engineering: chiller installation,
pressurised systems, ventilation refurbishment. FY24 revenue £28.8m,
EBITDA £5.2m (18.1% margin), +6.0% YoY. The highest-margin segment
on a project basis but lumpy: 65% of the segment's annual revenue
typically lands in two pricing windows (May/June, October/November)
tied to customer capex cycles.

The segment's pipeline at Q1 FY25 stood at £41m of identified
projects with a 52% conversion rate from prior-year cohorts —
implying £21.3m of FY25 revenue if conversion holds, vs FY24's
£28.8m. The pipeline read is the single biggest forecasting risk in
the deal.

### 2.4 Compliance Auditing (8% of revenue)

Statutory compliance audits (BAFE, Gas Safe, F-Gas, electrical EICR,
asbestos surveys). FY24 revenue £14.4m, EBITDA £3.2m (22.2%
margin), +11.0% YoY. The smallest segment but the highest-margin
and the fastest-growing. Recurring revenue model (95% of revenue
under multi-year retainer); regulatory tailwind from tightening
post-Grenfell building-safety legislation.

The Compliance segment is the only segment outperforming the
sector benchmark on margin (sector median 16-18%); attributable to
TargetCo's pre-2018 investment in a proprietary compliance tracking
platform that automates 70% of the audit workflow.

## 3. Customer concentration

Top-5 customers account for 31% of group revenue; top-10 account for
44%. The concentration is not extreme by UK industrial services
standards (peer group typically 35-50% top-10) but the deal
structure should account for the largest exposure:

> **The "Project Halo" account.** TargetCo holds a £18m/year
> facilities maintenance contract with a UK retail bank's 380-branch
> estate, signed in 2018 and up for renewal in **March 2026 (14
> months from CIM date)**. The bank has issued an open RFP. TargetCo
> is the incumbent, has a 4.6/5 service-quality NPS, and management
> believes renewal probability is "high but not certain". Loss of
> this contract would represent a ~10% revenue hit and ~14% EBITDA
> hit (the contract carries above-segment-average margin).

The buyer should treat the Halo renewal as the deal's binary risk
gate. Neither extending the renewal nor securing a backstop replaces
diligence on what the buyer would do if the renewal goes the other
way.

## 4. Geographic exposure

UK 91% (England 78%, Scotland 8%, Wales 4%, NI 1%); Republic of
Ireland 9%. Three of TargetCo's 12 operational sites are in
the UK; one is in Cork. The ROI footprint is sub-scale and has
historically been EBITDA-negative; FY24 was the first profitable
year (£0.4m EBITDA on £16.2m revenue). The buyer can either invest
to scale ROI (estimated £3-5m capex over 24 months) or divest the
ROI book; the segment has had two informal indicative bids in the
past 18 months at 0.6-0.8x revenue.

The 130bps margin expansion FY21→FY24 reflects (i) Compliance segment
mix gain, (ii) Mechanical Services pricing discipline post-supply-
chain reset, and (iii) ~£1.4m of recurring overhead reduction from
the FY22 finance-function consolidation.

### Working capital

Days sales outstanding (DSO) has improved meaningfully:

- FY21: 64 days
- FY22: 60 days
- FY23: 55 days
- FY24: 51 days (target 48 days by FY26)

The 13-day improvement was driven by a centralised credit-control
function set up in FY22 and the rollout of e-invoicing across the
top-50 customer set. Inventory turn is broadly flat (Industrial
Cleaning carries chemicals + consumables; the rest is light).

### Debt structure

Net debt £29.0m (1.21x LTM Adj EBITDA):

- £35.0m senior term loan (Lloyds), SONIA + 275bps, bullet maturity
  September 2026 (18 months from CIM date)
- £6.0m undrawn RCF (Lloyds, SONIA + 200bps)
- Cash £6.0m
- No subordinated debt; no PIK; no factoring exposure

The September 2026 maturity is inside the typical sponsor exit
window. The buyer should expect to refinance at signing or shortly
after; current pricing in the UK mid-cap leveraged loan market is
SONIA + 350-450 for similar credit profiles.

## 6. Operational footprint

12 sites: 3 freehold (Bristol HQ; Manchester depot; Birmingham
warehouse), 9 leased (regional service hubs across UK + Cork).
Aggregate leased footprint 184,000 sq ft; weighted-average lease
length 6.4 years.

Vehicle fleet: 312 vehicles (light commercial + service vans). 60%
leased on 4-year operating leases; 40% owned. Replacement cycle
running at 8 years (segment median 6) — a maintenance-capex risk
the buyer should price into the model.

IT infrastructure: ageing on-prem ERP (Microsoft Dynamics NAV 2017)
under active migration to Dynamics 365 Business Central. £4.0m
total capex committed across FY25-FY27, of which £1.4m incurred to
date. Migration is "amber" status: behind schedule by 4 months but
not flagged as a deal-breaker by management.

## 7. Management presentation Q&A

The buyer's deal team submitted 8 questions in advance of management
presentations. Excerpted responses:

**Q1: Project Halo renewal — what's the contingency plan if you
lose it?** *Management:* "We have a parallel pipeline of two
mid-sized retail-estate accounts (~£11m and £6m respectively) that
could absorb capacity within 9 months. Margin would compress
~80bps for two years during ramp."

**Q2: ESG positioning — net-zero commitments and exposure?**
*Management:* "Scope 1 + 2 reduction plan committed by 2030;
on-track. Customer-driven (Scope 3) is the larger exposure: 14% of
contracts now have explicit ESG-linked KPIs. Compliance segment
benefits; Cleaning segment occasionally exposed on solvent use."

**Q3: Contract renewal pipeline — top 20 customer renewals next 24
months?** *Management:* "£42m of contracted revenue up for renewal
in the FY25-FY26 window. Project Halo is the largest single
contract. Renewal probability across the cohort is estimated at
84% by management; an independent benchmarking firm put it at
78% in their FY24 review."

**Q4: Compliance segment margin — sustainable or peaking?**
*Management:* "Sustainable. The proprietary platform's
amortisation completes FY27, which actually adds 100bps. Margin
compression risk is from new entrants — three regional Compliance
specialists have raised growth equity in the last 18 months."

**Q5: Cleaning segment churn — what's behind the 2% growth?**
*Management:* "Slowdown is real. Two of our top 15 Cleaning
customers reduced spend in FY24 (manufacturing capacity
rationalisation). Pipeline conversion is healthy at 38% but
average deal size is shrinking ~6% YoY. We are exploring a
pharma-grade specialisation strategy that would shrink revenue
short-term and lift margin to 14-15% in 24-36 months."

**Q6: Capex plans — committed vs discretionary?**
*Management:* "Committed: £4.0m IT (Dynamics 365 migration), £1.6m
fleet replacement, £0.8m HQ refit, £0.4m HSE upgrades — total £6.8m
across FY25-FY27. Discretionary: £3-5m if ROI scale-up proceeds.
No segment-level expansion capex committed."

**Q7: Succession — CEO Ian Cartwright is 64. What's the plan?**
*Management:* "Ian intends to step back to non-executive Chairman
within 12-18 months. The Group Operations Director (Anita
Devereaux, 47, with TargetCo since 2015) is the internal
candidate. The board has not yet run an external search but is
willing to."

**Q8: Pension exposure — defined-benefit liabilities?**
*Management:* "Closed DB scheme, last open accrual 2009. IAS 19
deficit £8.0m at last triennial valuation (March 2023); recovery
plan running at £1.2m/year contribution to FY32. Not a material
deal-economics issue but the buyer should diligence the actuarial
assumptions independently."

## 8. Comparable transactions

Three plausible UK industrial-services comparables for valuation
triangulation. All synthetic — figures plausible but not real
deals.

| Target            | Acquirer                  | Year | EV (£m) | EV/EBITDA | Source                        |
|-------------------|---------------------------|------|---------|-----------|-------------------------------|
| Crestwood Group   | Sentinel Capital Partners | 2023 | 215     | 9.5x      | UK mid-cap Mergermarket DB    |
| Brighton FM Ltd   | Quantum Industrial        | 2023 | 142     | 8.1x      | Press release + intermediary  |
| Aldwych Compliance| Apex Holdings             | 2022 | 95      | 7.2x      | Industry analyst note Q3 FY23 |

Median EV/EBITDA: 8.1x (range 7.2-9.5x). The range is
sensitive to segment mix — Aldwych Compliance traded at the lower
end despite the highest growth profile, reflecting concentration risk
(top-3 customers 58% of revenue).

For TargetCo, applying the median to FY24 Adj EBITDA (£25.6m)
implies a base case EV of £207m. Adjusting for TargetCo's
diversification advantage (4 segments vs Aldwych's 1), Compliance
segment growth premium, and the Halo renewal risk — the buyer
should expect a defensible range of £205-235m.

## 9. Process

Bid deadlines and process detail are out-of-scope for this CIM;
managed by Lazard Mid-Market team. Indicative bid window opens 6
weeks from CIM circulation; final bids 8 weeks after that. The
sponsor's stated minimum acceptable price is undisclosed but
informally communicated as "north of £200m."
